# nagios_nna_suricata_ruleset (Resource)

Manages a Suricata ruleset in Nagios Network Analyzer's ruleset catalog: a downloadable collection of rules NNA fetches from a URL. NNA ships roughly 30 built-in rulesets; this resource creates additional custom ones, and can also adopt a built-in one via `terraform import` (destroying an imported built-in ruleset deletes it from the catalog).

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "nagios_nna_suricata_ruleset" "example" {
  name        = "myorg/custom"
  url         = "https://rules.example.com/custom.rules.tar.gz"
  description = "Internal detection rules"
  enabled     = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The ruleset's name (e.g. "myorg/custom"). Must be unique, and cannot be changed in place - Network Analyzer silently ignores a rename, so changing it replaces the ruleset.
- `url` (String) The URL NNA downloads the ruleset from. Network Analyzer does not validate it.

### Optional

- `description` (String) A human-readable description of the ruleset.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether NNA fetches and uses this ruleset.
- `secret_code` (String, Sensitive) The subscription/secret code for a commercial ruleset whose URL contains a secret-code placeholder. Network Analyzer stores and returns it in plaintext.

### Read-Only

- `id` (Number) The numeric ID Network Analyzer assigns this ruleset.
- `secret_code_required` (Boolean) Whether NNA considers a secret code mandatory for this ruleset. Server-assigned.
- `type` (String) The ruleset's origin as classified by NNA: "Custom" for rulesets created through the API, "Open" or "Commercial" for built-in ones.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by the numeric ruleset id (see GET /api/v1/suricata/rulesets).
terraform import nagios_nna_suricata_ruleset.example 31
```
